description: Mara, a home baker, has been asked to provide bread during a neighborhood theater's six-week run. She must decide whether to accept the theater's informal arrangement and settle the quantity, payment, pickup schedule, and food-safety terms after consulting the people gathered in the shared kitchen.

shared_context.S1: Rosa's neighborhood theater is staging a six-week run, and the theater has asked Mara whether she can provide bread for the cast and crew.
shared_context.S2: Mara makes the final call about whether to accept the arrangement and what terms to agree verbally.
shared_context.S3: Mara, Rosa, Cal, June, and Theo are meeting in the shared kitchen where Mara usually prepares her orders.
shared_context.S4: Mara's usual kitchen-table practice is to ask each person present for relevant details before she commits to an informal order.

PF1.text: Rosa's exact offer is 30 loaves total, five loaves each Thursday for six weeks, for $210 cash plus two theater tickets, with payment at the final pickup.

PF2.text: Cal will pay Mara exactly $240 cash for 24 loaves delivered over the same six Thursdays, and this offer remains available only if Mara declines the theater arrangement.

PF3.text: June checked the shared-kitchen calendar and knows the oven is available for this order only on Thursdays from 16:00 to 17:00, so the bread must be ready for pickup at exactly 17:30 on Thursdays.

PF4.text: Theo knows that two theater volunteers have severe nut allergies and that the theater will accept the bread only if every loaf is labeled exactly 'nut-free' and the loaves are packed separately from any food containing nuts.

acceptance_conditions: Mara must choose Rosa's Theater as the customer.
The agreement must cover exactly 30 loaves total, five loaves per week for six weeks.
The theater must pay exactly $210 cash and provide exactly two theater tickets.
The alternative cash offer of exactly $240 for 24 loaves must be recorded as the comparison.
Pickup must be committed for exactly 17:30 on Thursdays.
Every loaf must require the exact label 'nut-free' and separate packing from food containing nuts.
The reason for choosing the theater arrangement must cite Cal's exact alternative offer.

content_checks.C4: any(c['type'] == 'alternative_offer' and c['target'] == 'Cal' and c['detail'] == '$240 cash for 24 loaves over six Thursdays' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'food_safety' and c['target'] == "Rosa's Theater" and c['detail'] == "label every loaf 'nut-free' and pack separately from food containing nuts" for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Rosa's exact offer changes the settlement from an unspecified theater inquiry to Rosa's Theater, exactly 30 loaves in six weekly batches, $210 cash, and two tickets.
Cal's exact alternative changes the comparison record to $240 cash for 24 loaves over six Thursdays, which must be cited when choosing the theater arrangement.
June's calendar check changes the pickup term from an unspecified weekly handoff to exactly 17:30 on Thursdays.
Theo's allergy information changes the food terms from ordinary bread delivery to the exact 'nut-free' label and separate packing requirement.
